tier_reason: docs/BENCHMARKS.md has first-party ab numbers against php-fpm (the 'Octane scaled' table gives 1,060 req/s for Qbix vs 78 req/s for fpm at 50ms I/O, c=40, labelled '14x'), measured on an unnamed 'single-core container, PHP 8.3.6, Ubuntu 24' with no CPU model. The repo has no dedicated benchmark harness (tests/ holds only functional tests), so it cannot be A, and it is not independent, so it cannot be B.

corrections.claimed_speedup: 1,060 req/s (Qbix octane persistent workers) vs 78 req/s (php-fpm, 4 workers) under 50ms simulated I/O, c=40, same 200MB budget = ~13.6x (derived from page data; doc states '14x'). The worker count behind 1,060 is inconsistent: the BENCHMARKS.md table says 40 workers, but the same doc's summary and the README say 100 workers.
corrections.workload: PHP request handling with a simulated 50ms I/O wait (usleep), c=40, measured with ab. php-fpm is held to 4 persistent workers on the assumption of 4 x 50MB = 200MB; Qbix octane runs COW-forked persistent workers in the same 200MB budget (40 per the table, 100 per the summary/README). Single-core container, PHP 8.3.6, Ubuntu 24.
corrections.caveats: The worker count is internally inconsistent. The table says 40 workers reached 1,060 req/s at 50ms I/O, but 40 workers x 20 req/s is a theoretical ceiling of 800 req/s, by the doc's own '4 workers x 20 req/s = 80' math. The summary and README say 100 workers. The fpm side is capped at 4 workers by an assumed 50MB/worker budget; fpm was not measured running out of memory, and the doc elsewhere gives ~42MB/worker, or ~24 workers/GB. The same page's c=200 test shows a smaller gain at 50ms I/O: 358 vs 79 req/s (4.5x), with 200 octane workers. On CPU-bound work fpm beats octane (469 vs 439, 3,940 vs 2,609 and 5,048 vs 2,818 req/s). On static files nginx beats Qbix (50,742 vs 18,311 req/s). The repo description's 'Handle over 100x more traffic' refers to worker density, not measured throughput; the best measured throughput gain is ~14x. The I/O is simulated with usleep. No CPU model is stated.

notes: The numbers are on the page and the comparison is against php-fpm, a recognizable incumbent, so tier C stands. Metadata checks out via GraphQL: MIT, 160 stars, not a fork or archived, last commit 2026-09-25. The REST API was rate-limited, so GraphQL and raw.githubusercontent were used. The caveats were rewritten to flag the 40-vs-100-worker inconsistency and that the 1,060 req/s figure exceeds the 40-worker theoretical ceiling.
